A_open.text: October 31. The Great Hall is draped in cobwebs, paper bats, and two hundred cups of cheerful punch.
Full moon tonight. The note, the archive, Mr. Gourd. It has all been leading here.
At the entrance, Brad has one last decision to make: what to wear.

do.text: Straw in his collar, a floppy hat on his head. A crow tries to nest in the hat.
I'm not a bird's apartment. Shoo.
Black wings. A beak. The Homecoming mascot head, now much cleaner.
I earned this head. I knocked it off.
A fake beard, a flannel shirt, and a very serious squint.
Pumpkins don't wait.

A_open.text: The music swells. At the top of the stairs, Jane appears in a formal gown, a necklace at her throat.
Close your mouth. It's a dress, not a dragon.
Walk up to people and press Action. When you're ready, find the crow on the punch table.

do.text: Dad lent me Mom's necklace. He cried a little. Don't tell him I told you.
You look... I don't have a word. I have several. They're all bad.
That's the best compliment I've ever gotten.
I'm a goth dressed as a witch. It's a stretch. I'm disturbed by how little I changed.
You look great.
The tavern regulars bet I won't smile tonight. Don't make me lose money.
I'm a slice of pumpkin pie! Do you love it? I can't sit down!

then.text: The punch is one to four, like you said. I stirred it with a wooden spoon and a prayer.

else.text: The punch is extra glowy tonight! I think that's a good sign!
...That is not a good sign.

then.text: Mr. Bart. You know it's me. Please don't acknowledge it. The Dean thinks I'm an alumnus.
I carry two hundred vials of neutralizer. If the bloom gets out of hand, I'll need you.

else.text: Good evening. I am an alumnus. Gourd. Class of... a long time ago.
Mr. Gourd, you're wearing a trench coat to a Halloween dance.
It's a costume. I am dressed as a man in a trench coat.
It's very convincing.

do.text: Gord stands by the wall in his best flannel. A name tag reads: I'M A FARMER.

then.text: Is that my beard?
It's a tribute.
It's crooked.

do.text: Moon's up. The bloom comes at midnight. Don't drink the punch.
And Brad. Whatever happens tonight, stay close to the people you care about.

A2_crow.text: On the edge of the punch table, the crow waits. Something shiny glints in its beak.
It drops the object in Brad's palm. A name tag: BRAD BART (LEGACY!).
Thank you, Inspector. I forgive you.
Brad pins the tag on. The crow bobs once and flutters up into the rafters.

A3_dance.text: The band strikes up a slow waltz. Couples drift onto the floor.

then.text: Dance with me. I lead. I've always led. Dad says it's why I'm good with tractors.
I'll try not to step on you.
You will. It'll be adorable.
They sway. Brad steps on her foot exactly twice. She laughs both times.
I don't dance. I stand near people who dance.
One song?
...One song. If anyone films it, I'll end them.
She dances like a coat hanger. Halfway through, her mouth twitches.
In the crowd, someone groans and hands over money.
Can you dance with a pie? I can't hold you. I'd slide right off!
I'll improvise.
They manage a sort of sideways pie waltz. Crumbs fall in their wake. Dean Whitlock slips on one.

else.text: Mr. Bart. The proper term is wallflower. Shall we be wallflowers together?
They stand by the wall in the shadow of a paper bat, watching the dancers sway.
Twenty-five years ago my mother came home from this dance and never danced again.

B_bloom.text: Nine o'clock. The full moon crests the tall windows of the Great Hall.
A toast! To Ravenwood! And to anyone who can hear me over that humming!
A hum rises from every direction. The jack-o'-lanterns on the tables flare and begin to glow.
Three miles away, Patch Seven blooms. The pumpkins crack open and release glowing petals.
The wind carries them to town.
Petals drift through the vents. The punch bowl brightens until it is almost too bright to look at.

then.text: The glow is soft. Voices rise, but gently. Confessions drift through the room like leaves.
I never read the book. I just read the back.
I am mildly afraid of squirrels. Mildly.
I sometimes drive Dad's tractor to the donut shop. Sometimes.
I miss your father. I only read the first page of his letter.
People laugh, hug, and dance. It is the kindest chaos Ravenwood has ever seen.

else.text: I NEVER READ THE BOOK! ANY OF THEM!
I'M AFRAID OF SQUIRRELS! I HAVE BEEN SINCE 1987! THEY KNOW IT!
A freshman in a squirrel costume faints.
Two rival debate captains shout across the floor: 'I'VE LOVED YOU SINCE REGIONALS!' 'I KNOW!'
They kiss.
The band stops. The drummer: 'We don't actually know how to play. We know three songs. One is a lullaby.'
I HAVE LIED ABOUT QUIET HOURS FOR FORTY YEARS! THERE ARE NO QUIET HOURS!
I DRIVE DAD'S TRACTOR TO THE DONUT SHOP! EVERY WEDNESDAY!
I LIKE DANCING! THERE! IT'S TERRIBLE!
THE BLUE ONE WAS NOT BLUEBERRY! IT WAS BLUE CHEESE! AND SOMETHING ELSE!
I MISS YOUR FATHER! HE WROTE ELEVEN PAGES AND I ONLY READ ONE!

B_bloom.text: I miss my dad! I wish he were here!
A black shape swoops across the hall. It plucks the mustache off Mr. Gourd's lip and flies away.
YES! IT'S ME! I'VE BEEN BUYING PUMPKINS FOR THREE WEEKS! I WAS TRYING TO PREVENT THIS!
The whole hall gasps. Then, a beat later, applauds.
In the roar, one person catches Brad's eye.

C_j.text: Brad. Walk with me. Please. I need air. I need a lot of air.
Patch Seven in bloom. The pumpkins have opened like flowers. Glowing petals drift in the moonlight.
I love this farm. Every muddy inch of it. I'm not leaving.
And I want you to stay. For the winter. For Doris. For me.
I'm sorry. It's the bloom. I can't hold anything back.
Don't be sorry. I can't either.

then.text: Brad, I adore you. As a friend. I think you're not ready for the other thing. Not yet.

options.text: Not yet. I need to think

then.text: I feel the same. I'm staying. For Doris, for the winter, and for you.
Then stay.
Under the glowing petals, Jane kisses him. A pumpkin hums, very softly, in approval.
I feel the same. I really do.
Then let's take it slow. Ask me again after the harvest.
She squeezes his hand. It's a promise made of straw and moonlight.
Friends. Okay. Best friends. With pumpkin privileges.
She leans on his shoulder. It's warm, and a little bittersweet.

else.text: Not yet. I understand. The farm's door stays open.
So does mine.

C_s.text: At the center of the floor, Sandra stands frozen. A ring of Log & Stump regulars has formed around her.
Your terrible jokes. Your boots. How you lied for me in the library.
The tavern regulars burst into cheers. Someone throws a pretzel.
I am going to destroy this punch. With fire.
I can't stop saying things either. It's a terrible night for secrets.

then.text: You're a friend. Don't make it weird. I'm fine. I'll be fine.

else.prompt: Sandra covers her face with both hands.

options.text: Take her to the roof and confess

do.text: Brad leads her out of the crush, up a narrow stair, onto the roof of the Great Hall.
The moon is enormous. The hum seems very far away.

options.text: Not yet. I need to think

then.text: I think about you too. All the time. I'm staying. With you.
That's... the best news I've gotten in my life. Don't tell the regulars.
She kisses him, once, quickly, as if daring herself. Then she smiles. A real, full smile.
I think about you too. A lot.
Good. Let's go slowly. I'm easily startled.
Friends. Fine. The best friends are the ones who don't flinch.

else.text: Not yet. Understood. I can wait. I'm very good at waiting. And at grudges.

C_g.text: Georgia seizes Brad's hand and pulls him behind the dessert table, in her enormous pumpkin pie costume.
I can't stop talking! I want to bake in a city! A tiny bakery on a big street!
And I want you to come with me. I've wanted that since the cookie.

then.text: Brad pulls a crumpled envelope from his jacket. The pastry school application.
I brought it. In case.
You brought it?!
Oh no. I said too much. You're a lovely friend. Forget I said the other part.

else.prompt: Georgia is waiting, wide-eyed, in her pie.

options.text: Not yet. I need to think

then.text: I'll follow you anywhere. And I'll mail this tonight.
You absolutely have to eat my first croissant!
Georgia hugs him, pie costume and all. It's like being hugged by a very affectionate dessert.
I'd like that. Let's plan it. Slowly.
A plan! I love plans! I'll bake one.
Friends. Okay. Friends get free muffins. Friends get all the free muffins.

else.text: Not yet. That's fine. I'll hold on to the envelope. For when you're ready.

C_p.text: In the confusion, Patricia catches Brad's eye. She turns and walks toward the balcony. Brad follows.
The balcony. The roar of the hall falls away. Below, the quad is silver with moonlight.
My mother shut down the program after the dance. She blamed herself for twenty-five years.
I became a biologist to fix it. I've been terrified ever since.
I'm not brave, Mr. Bart. I'm only stubborn.
You saw through the mustache. I find that unsettling. And pleasant. Mostly unsettling.
Do you want to do the right thing? Stop the bloom? End it, once and for all?
Let's decide together. In a minute.

then.text: Mr. Bart. I am your professor. The candor has made me say too much. You'll forget it.

else.prompt: Patricia waits, hands clasped, very still.

options.text: Not yet. I need to think

then.text: Professor. I care about you. A lot. I know the rules. I'm willing to wait.
Ask me again in December. After grades are filed.
She smiles. It is the most beautiful, terrifying smile Brad has ever seen.
Professor. I care about you. I know the rules.
Ask me again in spring. When I've stopped being your professor.
Thank you, Mr. Bart. For being a friend. I haven't had many.

else.text: Of course. When you know. Or not at all. Either is acceptable.

D_close.text: Midnight. The moon is at its height. Everyone in the hall glows a little.
Gord crosses the floor like a man crossing a river.
Brad. I wrote the note. I made a promise to your father.
I never wanted to lie to you. I wanted to keep you out of it.
What was the promise?
Your dad should be the one to tell you. He's coming for Thanksgiving.
He's coming?
I called him last night. He cried. Then he said he was in a meeting.
I have the neutralizer. Two hundred vials. It will end the bloom, and the pumpkins, and tonight.
Your father isn't here. His boots are. It's your call.

D_close.prompt: The pumpkins hum. The whole hall waits.

do.text: End it. Safely. Before someone gets hurt.
Vials go into the punch bowl and out the window. The hum slows. The glow dims.
Three miles away, Patch Seven sighs. The hall is quiet. Everyone remembers everything they said.
While the others look away, Gord quietly pockets a single seed.

options.text: Let the town be honest tonight

do.text: Let them have tonight. It's one night of truth. It might do some good.
That is... unscientific.
It's right.
Next year's dance will have a warning poster! And a squirrel-free zone!
The dance goes on. By half past midnight the glow fades. Mrs. Alder dances with the Dean.
Nobody ever speaks of it again.

D_close.text: In the moonlight, the crow rises from the roof carrying a single pumpkin seed. Brad watches it go.
Late. Brad and Gord walk the farm road home under the moon.

then.text: Jane: Home safe? Dad says you cried. I told him you didn't.
Sandra: Made it home. Don't text back. (Please text back.)
Georgia: Home safe?? I made forty croissants at 2 AM! Come eat!

else.text: Patricia: Mr. Bart. Please get some sleep. You have class tomorrow. -P.P.

D_close.text: Your father's letter. Eleven pages.
You read the first.
Read the second tonight. Between dances.
What did it say?
That he's proud. That he's sorry. And that you should wear a hat.

then.text: The patch is quiet. First time in twenty-five years.

else.text: The patch is still glowing. I'll sit up with it.

D_close.text: I'm glad I came here, Uncle Gord.
Me too, boy.
A month later. Thanksgiving. The first snow.
